_about: The meeting vocabulary as DATA. Concept-centred, not people-centred (user decision, Sep 4 2026): keywords and decisions are what the semantic layer is for; who said them is thin attribution. A Meeting is PROVENANCE, not a container — which is why RaisedIn points FROM the durable thing TO its evidence. That direction is what lets a WorkItem become the hub later without re-parenting anything: a decision simply gains a second RaisedIn edge. Nothing in code knows any of these names.

natures.concept: The knowledge itself — what is being talked about and decided on.
natures.commitment: Something the organisation is now accountable for.
natures.provenance: Where a concept or commitment came from — evidence, not ownership.
natures.party: A human, referenced only to attribute a commitment.

pii.none: No personal data; any property may be written.
pii.identifying: Names a real human. Only a label and the kind of id may be written — never an address.

Concept.definition: A thing the organisation talks about and decides on — a capability, a system, a policy, a term of art. Durable and shared: the same concept in two meetings is the same node.

Decision.definition: A settled choice about one or more concepts. Durable: it happened to be raised in a meeting, and may later be raised against a work item.
Decision.confusable_with: An ActionItem is work someone owes; a Decision is a choice already made.

ActionItem.definition: Work one person owes, about one or more concepts, often carrying out a decision.
examples: Draft the migration plan by 12 Oct
Confirm the licence count with the vendor

Meeting.definition: One recorded conversation. Evidence for the concepts and commitments that reference it — never their owner.

Person.definition: A human, referenced only to attribute a decision or own an action. Deliberately thin: the semantic layer is knowledge, not a directory.

Concerns.definition: This commitment is about that concept — the core edge of the model.

Resolves.definition: A later decision revises or supersedes an earlier one.

Implements.definition: An action item carries out a decision.

BroaderThan.definition: A concept generalises another — the term hierarchy, when one emerges.

RaisedIn.definition: PROVENANCE: where this was first recorded. Points FROM the durable thing TO its evidence, never the reverse — so a work item can become a second target without moving anything.

Attended.definition: A person was present at a meeting.

rules: Every Decision and every ActionItem must Concern at least one Concept — that is what makes the model concept-centred rather than a pile of minutes.
A Meeting is never the source of a relation: provenance points from the durable thing to its evidence, so adding a WorkItem later is an extra RaisedIn target and not a re-parenting.
A Person carries a label and the kind of id only. An address is never written into the graph.
